source.reason: b0039 describes the dislocation reaction producing straight sessile ⟨100⟩ edge locks in Fe–28% Al (Figs. 12–13).

interaction_type.value: reaction of two (1/2)⟨111⟩ superdislocations producing a sessile ⟨100⟩ edge dislocation lock

qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: Imaging the reactions (marked r) with many g vectors confirms a reaction of two superdislocations with different ⟨111⟩ Burgers vectors lying in different {110} glide planes, producing a pair of edge dislocations with ⟨100⟩ Burgers vector in a sessile configuration on a cube plane. For example, the reaction [111] + [1̄11] formed a pair of [100] edge dislocations along the [010] direction, hence lying in a (001) plane. Such configurations constitute locks that prevent further room-temperature superdislocation motion.

slip_behavior.value: Dislocations are generally straight and mostly in near-screw orientations; large numbers of rather straight superdislocations of several different Burgers vectors, often oriented in near-screw directions along their {110} glide planes. Superdislocations composed of two (1/2)⟨111⟩ partials glide as individual dislocations and trail APBII faults; they do not trail any APBI faults.

interface_notes.value: The two (1/2)⟨111⟩ partials constitute a perfect superdislocation for the B2 lattice but an imperfect superdislocation for the DO3 lattice, hence trail APBII faults as they glide (observed when imaging with g = (1/2)(1/2)(1/2) in B2 convention or 111 in DO3 convention). These superdislocations do not trail APBI faults (confirmed with 100-type g vector).

source.reason: b0024 and b0012 describe the compression testing and work-hardening-rate measurement for the studied alloys including Fe–28% Al.

measurement_conditions.value: Room temperature, to 2–3% strain at a nominal strain rate of 3×10⁻⁴ s⁻¹

purpose.value: Measure stress–strain behaviour and work hardening rate

key_findings.value: Smooth onset of plasticity, no discrete yield points, always slightly curved stress–strain behaviour; work hardening rate measured as the secant over the 1–1.5% strain range.

unmapped_findings: The work hardening rate peak of the Fe–28% Al alloy coincides with a strong peak in the elastic anisotropy (Zener factor A reaching between 6 and 7 around 28–30% Al); the peak is attributed to high Peierls forces (core effects) rather than to the elastic anisotropy itself.

The small ductility maximum of Fe–28% Al (~5–6%) is explained by the Considère criterion as arising from the high work hardening rate over the 26–30% Al range where the flow stress is relatively constant.

No APB tubes were observed in the Fe–28% Al alloy; the higher work hardening of the ordered state is attributed to the formation of superdislocation dipole locks and the increased tendency of dislocations to lie in screw orientations.

For the Fe–28% Al alloy, reaction of different ⟨111⟩ superdislocations to produce straight sessile ⟨100⟩ edge dislocations (Peierls forces extremely high at room temperature) creates strong barriers to further glide of ⟨111⟩ superdislocations, potentially contributing to the high work hardening.
